note: Each program PARSES cleanly (thermite-syntax accepts the syntax — combinator calls are generic call exprs) but the thermite-spec validator must REJECT it with the named SpecError variant, because it steps outside the SpecTherm cage (§4.2). Hand-derived (R-CHAR-3). The `expected` variant names mirror .design/spec/spectherm-combinators.md REQ-4; the builder may rename variants but the REJECT outcome + the cause must hold.

cases.name: unknown_combinator
cases.program: fn f(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 req frobnicate(xs) ens result == 0 fx pure { 0 }
cases.why: frobnicate is not a registered combinator and not a declared spec fn — an arbitrary free-function call is forbidden in a contract (§4.2 locked cage).

cases.name: wrong_arity
cases.program: fn f(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 req sorted(xs, xs) ens result == 0 fx pure { 0 }
cases.why: sorted has arity 1; called with 2 args.

cases.name: wrong_arg_kind
cases.program: fn f(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 req true ens forall_in(xs, 5) fx pure { 0 }
cases.why: forall_in's 2nd arg must be a predicate closure (Pred); a literal 5 is not a closure.

cases.name: forall_below_wrong_arity
cases.program: fn f(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 req true ens forall_below(xs, |x| x < 5) fx pure { 0 }
cases.why: forall_below has arity 3 (Slice, Index, Pred); called with 2 (missing the Index).
